name: Cup with Handle

card.context: A leader that has already run at least 30% rests in a rounded base read on the weekly chart, above its 200-day, with RS 80 or more and growing sales. First or second base. Green or Yellow market, best at the start of a new uptrend.
card.pattern: A smooth U, 7 to 65 weeks long and 12% to 33% deep, climbs back near the old high, then dips into a handle: 5 days or more, drifting sideways to down in the upper half on lighter volume, holding the 50-day, tight at the end.
card.trigger: BASE BREAKOUT: price trades through the handle's high during regular hours, bought at market, no more than 4% past it. The in-handle shakeout is the owner's lower-risk way in.
card.stop: A few cents under the buy day's low or the prior day's, usually within about 3%; never wider than a few cents under the handle low.
card.failure_mode: A wedging or deep handle, a V-shaped cup or a late base breaks out and fades back through the pivot to the stop. 62% of cup breakouts throw back to the pivot within 30 days, so the day's-low stop is tested often.

criteria.statement: The stock rose at least 30% from its lowest low of the prior 6 months (120 sessions) to the left-side high.

measure.what: left-side high / lowest low of the prior 120 sessions - 1

options.basis: IBD's 30% (S7, S1); the 120-session window is the dossier's proposal, from the screener
the glossary's canonical window for every base (from dossier 01)

criteria.evidence: The scan used 30% over 120 sessions; the ten examples ran 31% to 72% before the cup. AAII 2015 and Stockbee repeat O'Neil, so they are not independent.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
criteria.evidence: The scanner has no RS test (its rs_trend is an absolute trend). Not coded in the scan.

criteria.statement: Growing sales and earnings preferred; the chart comes first.
criteria.evidence: IBD's CAN SLIM; the owner on RBRK: For CANSLIM checks all the boxes.

criteria.statement: First or second base since the last real correction; a third or later base is graded down.

measure.what: bases since the last real correction

criteria.evidence: Not coded in the scan. WDAY 2021-09-22, a 30-week cup with the handle resting on the 50-day, failed at 0.0R: a late, tired base is the filter the scan cannot apply.

criteria.statement: Find and measure the base on the weekly chart; time the buy on the daily.

options.basis: weekly base, daily trigger: IBD counts weeks (S1); about half the owner's cups are weekly reads (S36)
daily only
both as separate versions

criteria.evidence: The scan ran on daily bars with weeks counted as 5 sessions.

criteria.statement: Price above the 200-day SMA at the buy.
criteria.evidence: 20 of the 100 draft bank cup items were below their 200-day at the breakout. Chart IQ can still pass a stock under its 200-day.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.
criteria.evidence: Bracco's SIDU ($5) would fail it. The scan used the house floor over 2,630 names.

criteria.statement: The position is at most 1% of average daily volume.
Green market: full risk. Yellow: smaller and fewer. Orange: A+ only. Red: mostly cash and shorts.
criteria.evidence: Zanger: the best cups come at the beginning of a market move after a good correction, not at the end of a major advance (S17). Not coded in the scan.

criteria.statement: A cue, not a rule: best at the start of a new market uptrend after a correction, with the group leading and several of its stocks setting up.
criteria.evidence: Zanger (S17); the unsigned XLV note judged the group by how many of its stocks were setting up (S36).

criteria.statement: At least 7 weeks (35 sessions) from the left-side high to the day before the breakout, the handle included.

measure.what: sessions from the left-side high to the day before the breakout

options.basis: IBD: a proper cup base needs to span a minimum of seven weeks (S2, S7)
IBD's cup-without-handle column: a cup can be as short as six weeks (S5)

criteria.evidence: The scan used 35 sessions; the examples ran 7.6 (WPM) to 21.6 weeks (MCO). Daily or hourly mini cups under 7 weeks are flags or tight ranges (D-002, 04:2).

criteria.statement: At most 65 weeks (325 sessions).

measure.what: sessions from the left-side high to the day before the breakout

options.basis: IBD (S1, S7) and Bulkowski (S26): 7 to 65 weeks
a middle cap
the scanner's 65 daily bars (cup_handle_uct.py)

criteria.evidence: The scanner cannot see most of the cups IBD calls best (it caps at 13 weeks). WDAY's 30-week cup failed; MCO's 21.6-week cup ran 8.5R.

criteria.statement: Best between 3 and 6 months (63 to 126 sessions), symmetric; very long or lopsided cups grade down.

measure.what: sessions from the left-side high to the day before the breakout

criteria.evidence: IBD: most outstanding cup patterns will last between three and six months (S5).

criteria.statement: Depth from the left-side high to the cup's lowest intraday low: 12% to 33% in a normal market. 33% to 35% is allowed but graded down.

measure.what: (left-side high - lowest intraday low of the cup) / left-side high

options.value: 12% to 33%, 50% only after a bear market
options.basis: IBD (S2, S7, S5)
IBD's own 35% ceiling (S7, S6)
Zanger (S17)

criteria.recommended: 12% to 33%, 50% only after a bear market
criteria.evidence: The scan allowed 12% to 35% with the low in the middle 60% of the cup. The examples ran 12.1% (AAPL) to 21.3% (MCO). 9 of the 100 draft bank items are deeper than 33%, 7 deeper than 35%.

criteria.statement: Up to 50% deep only for a cup formed in a bear market.

measure.what: (left-side high - lowest intraday low of the cup) / left-side high
measure.note: only when the cup formed in a bear market

criteria.evidence: IBD: in bear markets, cups can run as deep as 50% (S5). Not coded in the scan.

criteria.statement: The cup falls no more than about 2.5 times the index's decline over the same weeks.

measure.what: cup depth / the index's decline over the same weeks

criteria.evidence: IBD calls 1.5 to 2.5 times the market's correction normal for growth stocks (S5); using 2.5 as the ceiling is the dossier's proposal. Not coded in the scan.

criteria.statement: A rounded U, not a V: at least 30% of the cup's bars have their low in the cup's bottom quarter.

measure.what: share of the cup's bars whose low sits in the bottom quarter of the cup's range

criteria.evidence: U not V is IBD's (S1, S5) and the consensus (Bulkowski S26, StockCharts S30, AAII S31); the 30% bottom-quarter test is the scanner's own U-versus-V check. EFX spent two months of lows in the bottom quarter.

criteria.statement: At most two weeks inside the cup with a high-to-low range of 10% or more.

measure.what: weeks inside the cup whose high-to-low range is 10% or more of price

criteria.evidence: IBD: no jagged edges or many wild weekly swings of 10% to 15% or more (S3); the count of two is the dossier's. ULTA 2016-12-16 had exactly two heavy weeks inside the cup and faded to the stop at 0.9R: the ceiling is the maximum, not the grade.

criteria.statement: Down weeks on the left side roughly match up weeks on the right.
criteria.evidence: IBD 2013-02-04 (S3). A cue; FFIV is the symmetric example.

criteria.statement: The right side climbs back to within about 10% of the left-side high before the handle starts.
criteria.evidence: IBD says the handle forms in the upper half (S7); Zanger puts the handle about 5% below the old high (S17). The scan used a right rim within 10% below (or 5% above) the left-side high.

criteria.statement: The handle is at least 5 sessions long.
criteria.evidence: IBD: if it is shorter than five days, it is not a handle (S8). 40 of the 100 draft bank items have handles under 5 sessions. The examples ran 5 (AX) to 19 days (MCO).

criteria.statement: Usually 1 to 4 weeks; a handle over about 22 sessions is graded down.
criteria.evidence: AAII and StockCharts 1 to 4 weeks, Zanger 4 days to 3 weeks; IBD wants more than one or two weeks (S8); Bulkowski: handles shorter than his median 22 days did better (S26). The 22-day grade-down is the dossier's.

criteria.statement: The handle falls at most 12% from its own high.

options.basis: IBD: usually no more than 8% to 12% (S6)
Zanger (S17)

options.value: a third of the cup's depth

criteria.evidence: The scan used 3% to 12% (under 3% is a flat shelf, not a handle). The examples' handles ran 3.0% to 6.7%. The scanner caps the handle at half the cup's depth, which allows 17.5% on a 35% cup.

criteria.statement: A handle of 8% or less is better; about 5% is best.
criteria.evidence: Leans on Zanger's about 5% below the old high (S17) and IBD's 8% to 12% (S6). Nine of the ten examples had handles under 7%.

criteria.statement: The handle's midpoint (halfway between its high and low) sits above the cup's midpoint.

measure.what: handle midpoint against the cup's midpoint

criteria.evidence: IBD 2015-09-11 gives the midpoint test (S7); handles that form too low present added risk of failure. The scan required it.

criteria.statement: A handle in the upper third of the base, within about 5% of the old high, is better.

measure.and: handle high within 5% of the left-side high

criteria.evidence: AAII 2015: upper half or third (S32); Minervini's 2020-05-13 post describes one chart's handle in the upper third, not a stated rule (S21); Zanger's about 5% below the old high (S17). RRC's handle sat in the upper third just under the rim.

criteria.statement: The handle's lows drift sideways to down: a straight line fitted through the handle's daily lows slopes flat or down. Rising lows (a wedge) is not a handle.

measure.what: slope of a least-squares line through the handle's daily lows

criteria.evidence: IBD: stocks with wedging handles have a higher failure rate (S8); a wedging handle with no shakeouts is a sign to steer clear (S9). The slope test is the screener's and the dossier's. The owner on ANET: inside day to avoid wedging up behavior.

criteria.statement: The handle's average daily volume is below the cup's average daily volume. Some very quiet days near the handle low is a grade cue, not a gate.
criteria.evidence: IBD gives the direction, no number (S2, S8). The examples' handles ran 0.63x (CNC) to 0.97x (RRC) of the cup's volume: RRC is the cue at its weakest acceptable.

criteria.statement: The handle holds above the 50-day line: no daily close below the 50-day SMA during the handle.

measure.what: daily closes in the handle below the 50-day SMA

criteria.evidence: IBD: a handle should generally form above the 50-day or 10-week moving averages (S8); the one-close test is the dossier's. WDAY's handle rested on the 50-day rather than well above it and failed.

criteria.statement: Tight at the end: the last 5 handle closes sit within about 3% of each other.

measure.what: (highest - lowest of the last 5 handle closes) / lowest

criteria.evidence: IBD: areas of tight trading, no number (S9); the owner's 3 weeks tight and double inside days (S36). The glossary's default tightness is a 0.85 range ratio; this card keeps the fixed 3% spread. Scan: the 274 hits that passed it did a little better, 32.1% to 3R and 24.8% to 5R, against 30.3% and 22.6% for all.

criteria.statement: The pivot is the highest price in the handle. For a cup without a handle, the left-side high. IBD adds 10 cents; with market orders the 10 cents does not matter.

measure.value: highest intraday high of the handle

criteria.evidence: IBD (S6, S7) and Zanger (S17) buy as price trades through the handle high; the cup without a handle buys the left-side high (S5). Bulkowski and AAII use a close above the rim, a later moment.

criteria.statement: How far past the handle high the buy point sits: a cent over (the Kicker plan), IBD's 10 cents, or at market as soon as it trades through.

measure.what: buy point offset above the handle high
value: at market as it trades through

options.basis: the Kicker plan's cent over the level
IBD (S6, S7)

options.value: at market as it trades through
options.basis: E57 market orders; D-003's default

criteria.recommended: at market as it trades through
criteria.evidence: The scan filled at the pivot plus a cent, or at the open when it gapped over the pivot.

criteria.statement: Price trades above the pivot during regular hours. Buy with a market order.
criteria.evidence: Market orders are E57. The scanner's close on 1.5x the 20-bar volume is not the house trigger. Scan: SCHW 2024-11-06 and KMI 2016-09-08 gapped over the pivot and never traded above the open fill.

criteria.statement: No buy more than 4% above the pivot.
criteria.evidence: IBD's buy zone is 5% (S12); the house 4% wins.

criteria.statement: At entry, no more than 10% above the 10-day average.
criteria.evidence: A fresh breakout from a handle is usually near its 10-day; it catches late chases.

criteria.statement: No new buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
criteria.evidence: 13 scan hits triggered on an earnings-reaction day and were set aside as a different setup (D-025).

criteria.statement: Volume on the trigger day: on pace for at least 40% above the 50-day average (1.4x) by the close. If the day closes with less, it is a warning, not an exit. For a cup without a handle, heavy volume matters more.

options.basis: required at 40% over the 50-day average: IBD (S6), AAII's 50-day baseline (S31)
a warning only, graded, since we buy at market intraday: the dossier's recommendation; D-006's default
no volume rule

criteria.evidence: GWW (0.73x) and EFX (0.78x) both ran 7.3R on light volume; FFIV (2.71x) and WB (2.99x) ran 41R and 32R; BX broke out on 4.9x and still stopped. IBD once called 38% barely sufficient (S4). The scan did not cut on volume.

criteria.statement: A cup without a handle is a variant inside this lesson: the pivot is the left-side high, bought especially when the stock takes out that high in heavy trade.

options.basis: a variant inside the Cup lesson: the dossier's recommendation; D-002's default
its own setup

criteria.evidence: IBD 2013-10-03 (S5). The unsigned XLV note: either handles out or becomes a powerful cup without handle breakout (S36).

criteria.statement: The owner's lower-risk buy inside the handle: a tight day, an inside day, or a shakeout that undercuts an earlier handle low and reclaims it (red to green), with every pattern line true. The pivot breakout still confirms the trade.

options.basis: the breakout over the handle high only
the in-handle shakeout or mid range cheat only
both: the breakout as the definition, the in-handle buy as our execution: the dossier's recommendation; D-027's default

criteria.evidence: The owner: buying those shakeouts is the optimal RR; a red to green move to show presence of buyers (S36). IBD: most successful handles feature a shakeout (S9). It is what makes the house 3% stop possible on this pattern. Not measured in the scan.

criteria.statement: The 3-C or mid range cheat: an earlier buy on a pause in the lower to middle third of the base. An earlier, riskier read of the same base; if taught, a separate advanced lesson.
criteria.evidence: Minervini: the cheat area develops in the lower to middle third of the base (S21); low cheats can be up to 8% below the 50-day (S24). The owner's BWXT mid range cheat entry (S36). Minervini's book rules were not read.

criteria.statement: A few cents under the low of the buy day, or of the prior day.

measure.value: a few cents under the buy day's low or the prior day's low

criteria.evidence: F62 gives the few cents. The scan used 5 cents under the lower of the trigger day's and the prior day's low, or the trigger day's low alone if that was wider than 3%.

criteria.statement: The stop should sit within about 3% of the buy. If the honest stop is wider, wait for a tighter spot (a quiet day near the pivot, an in-handle shakeout), size down from the stop, or skip. Never move the stop closer to make it fit.

options.basis: house default only (A3, F62)
the handle low as the stop, sized down
house default with the handle low as the outer limit: the dossier's recommendation

criteria.evidence: The examples' stops sat 0.7% (FFIV) to 3.0% (CNC) under the fill; the scan's median was about 2.3%. BX 2019-11-26: a 1.2% stop reached 2.4R in two sessions, then one dip took it before the stock made new highs; the house answer is the breakeven move at 2R to 5R, not a wider stop.

criteria.statement: Never wider than a few cents under the handle low: below the handle low the setup has failed. IBD's 7% to 8% loss limit is a reference, not ours.

measure.value: a few cents under the handle low

criteria.evidence: Bulkowski puts the stop at the handle low (S26); IBD sells at 7% or 8% below cost (S10, S12). The scanner's handle low times 0.985 gave 8.2% and 16.1% stops in the probe, far wider than A13.

criteria.statement: A real stop order with the broker. It only moves up.
criteria.evidence: A4: the stop only moves up.

criteria.statement: A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if that is past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 3R.
criteria.evidence: MCO reached 3R in 4 sessions and FFIV the next day; CNC, a slow mover, took 29 sessions.

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 5R.
criteria.evidence: All ten examples reached 5R. WB gapped higher the week after 5R: the case for holding the last third.

criteria.statement: If it opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
Trail the last third: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, under the 21-day for a steadier one.
criteria.evidence: AX reached 5R in about 7 weeks, then rolled over below the pivot: the example for trailing the last third under the 21-day.

criteria.statement: A climax run (Bracco's parabolic burst): sell a big part into it.
Time stop: still under 1R after 10 trading days, sell.

options.basis: C33 as written: D-019's default
more time for cups: Bulkowski found 62% of cup breakouts throw back within 30 days (S26); IBD gives breakouts more time

criteria.evidence: Nine of the ten examples were above 1R by the tenth session; CNC (3R in 29 sessions) and the scan's slow winners are the case for more time. The scan did not apply a time stop.

criteria.statement: 62% of cup breakouts come back to the breakout price within 30 days (Bulkowski). The day's-low stop will be tested often; that is normal, not a reason to widen it.

measure.what: throwback rate, Bulkowski's cup with handle, bull market

criteria.evidence: Bulkowski also found 47% of cups dropped substantially within two months of the breakout and 23% rose no more than 15% (S26). In the scan 85% of hits touched the stop at some point in 60 sessions; 197 of 403 never reached 1R.

criteria.statement: Before the buy: the handle's midpoint sits below the cup's midpoint, or the handle falls more than 12% from its own high.

measure.or: handle midpoint below the cup's midpoint

criteria.statement: Before the buy: the handle's lows rise (wedging), or the handle is shorter than 5 days.

measure.or: a rising line through the handle's lows

criteria.statement: Before the buy: volume rises through the handle.
Before the buy: a close below the 50-day during the handle.

measure.what: close against the 50-day SMA during the handle

criteria.evidence: IBD: should generally form above the 50-day (S8); treating one close as the disqualifier is the dossier's.

criteria.statement: Before the buy: the cup is a V, or deeper than 35% outside a bear market.

measure.what: (left-side high - lowest intraday low of the cup) / left-side high
measure.or: fewer than 30% of the cup's bars with lows in the bottom quarter

criteria.statement: Before the buy: the handle runs past about 6 weeks (30 sessions) with no breakout; the base is getting stale.
criteria.evidence: The scan allowed handles of 5 to 30 sessions. Bulkowski: shorter handles did better (S26).

criteria.statement: Before the buy: the market reading turns Red.
After the buy, the stop is the exit.
criteria.evidence: The owner: my stop is my stop most of the time (2026-11-09). CMG-style failures with nothing wrong in the setup are why the stop, not an opinion, is the exit.

criteria.statement: After the buy, a close back into the handle is a warning, not an exit by itself.
criteria.evidence: The owner struck the rule cut at least half if the stock falls back into its base (2026-11-09, rule 15). WDAY 2021-09-22 closed near its high on the breakout day, then fell straight through the stop.

a_plus: ch.prior_trend: 30% or more in a few months, on rising volume and RS
ch.cup_depth: 12% to 25%, under 2.5 times the market's drop
ch.shape_u: a smooth U, no 10% to 15% weekly swings
ch.handle_upper_third: upper third, within about 5% of the old high
ch.handle_drift: drifts down, a shakeout of an earlier low, tight closes at the end
ch.leadership: RS 80 or more, a leading group, growing sales and earnings
ch.market_reading: Green, early in a new uptrend
b_minus: ch.shape_no_wild_weeks: jagged, V-ish, two violent weeks inside (ULTA)
ch.handle_length_typical: over a month, or barely 5 days
ch.handle_drift: wedges up, loose, no shakeout
ch.leadership: RS lower, a lagging group
ch.market_reading: Yellow, late in a long run
ch.stop_width: the honest stop wider than 3%
no_trade: ch.inv_v_or_deep: a V, or deeper than 35% outside a bear market
ch.inv_handle: the handle below the cup's midpoint or deeper than 12%
ch.inv_wedge_or_short: a wedging handle, or under 5 days
ch.inv_close_under_50: a close under the 50-day in the handle
ch.cup_length_min: under 7 weeks (a flag or a tight range, not this setup)
ch.no_chase: more than 4% past the pivot
ch.stop_outer_limit: the honest stop below the handle low; never pull it in
ch.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day

lookalikes.tell: Measure the depth and the shape. A flat base falls 15% or less and stays boxy with a flat ceiling tapped at least twice; a cup falls 12% to 33% in a rounded U and then dips again into a handle before the buy.

Count the pullbacks. A cup is one rounded decline whose right side climbs back within 10% of the old high, then one handle at the rim; a VCP shows two or more separate pullbacks, each smaller than the last, and its pivot may sit well under the base high.

Measure the run before the rest. A high tight flag nearly doubles (90% or more in 8 weeks or less) and pauses 5 to 30 sessions with no rounded decline; a cup follows a 30% run and takes at least 7 weeks to round out and handle.

Count the weeks. A flag is a 3 to 15 session drift right after a 20% pole; a daily or hourly mini cup under 7 weeks is a flag or a tight range, not a cup, and a handle only counts after a cup of 7 weeks or more.

invalidations: Before the buy: the handle's midpoint sits below the cup's midpoint, or the handle falls more than 12% (ch.inv_handle).
Before the buy: the handle's lows rise, or the handle is under 5 days (ch.inv_wedge_or_short).
Before the buy: volume rises through the handle (ch.inv_volume_rises).
Before the buy: a close below the 50-day during the handle (ch.inv_close_under_50).
Before the buy: a V-shaped cup, or deeper than 35% outside a bear market (ch.inv_v_or_deep).
Before the buy: the handle runs past 30 sessions with no breakout (ch.inv_stale_handle).
Before the buy: the market reading turns Red (ch.inv_market_red).
Before the buy: a report within 3 sessions, wait (ch.earnings_window).
After the buy: the stop is the exit (ch.after_entry_stop).
After the buy: a close back into the handle is a warning, not an exit by itself (ch.close_back_in_handle).
mistakes: Buying a V-shaped recovery and calling it a cup.
Buying a handle in the lower half of the base.
Buying a handle that wedges up (the owner on ANET: inside day to avoid wedging up behavior).
Calling a 2 or 3-day dip a handle; under 5 days it is not one.
Chasing more than 4% past the pivot or more than 10% over the 10-day.
Buying a breakout on weak volume and ignoring it.
Trading a third or fourth-stage base like a first.
Using the handle low as the stop at full size, then taking an 8% to 12% loss.
Buying in a correction because the chart looks great.
Holding a failed breakout and hoping, or widening the stop.
Treating the measured-move target as a sure thing; Bulkowski found only 61% reach it.
Calling an hourly mini cup the same setup as a 7-week weekly base.

short_mirror.note: The inverted cup with handle, D47 mirrored (dossier 8.6): a rounded top, a small weak bounce (the handle) and a break below the handle low, only below the 200-day SMA (B26), RS 20 or less in a weak group (C31 mirror), shorted at market as price trades under the handle low with the stop a few cents over that day's high. Our app has detectors/classical/inverse_cup_handle.py. Bulkowski's numbers are worse than the long's (18% break-even failure, 17% average decline, 556 trades). IBD teaches no short cup. Whether to build a lesson is D-001 (04:11); the dossier says not until the owner asks.

best_conditions: A Green market reading, Yellow at smaller size; best at the start of a new market uptrend after a correction (Zanger), when the group is leading and several of its stocks are setting up. IBD: cups form during intermediate declines in the general market, so the breakout often comes as the market turns.

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.time_stop: under 1R after 10 trading days, sell (C33); whether cups get more time is D-019
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.climax: sell a big part into a climax run (C34)
management.earnings: hold through a report only if up 5R (B22)
management.overrides: none. The dossier (8.4) finds nothing setup-specific is needed. Not ours: IBD's sell most at 20% to 25% and its 8-week hold, Bulkowski's 61% of the cup's height, the scanner's full-height target. Bulkowski's 62% throwback rate is a lesson note: the stop gets tested, it does not get widened.

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop, no trims, no breakeven, no trail, no time stop; triggers from 2001-02-21 to 2026-11-02; one hit per name per 30 sessions; 2,630 liquid names

earnings_reaction_triggers.note: set aside as a different setup (D-025)

failures.why: a 10-week, 18%-deep cup, a 5-day handle, breakout on 4.9x volume, the heaviest in the scan; it reached 2.4R on the second session, then a one-day dip on the fifth session touched the 1.2% stop and the stock made new highs without us. A very tight trigger-day stop is cheap but fragile; the house answer is the breakeven move at 2R to 5R (B19), not a wider stop.
failures.stopped: stopped 4 sessions after the buy, 2019-12-03, low 51.78

failures.why: a 16-week, 19%-deep cup after a 76% run with an 8-day handle, at a glance the FFIV chart; inside the cup were a 10%-range week (the scan counts one; the rule allows two) and heavy-volume days, and the breakout faded within days to the stop with a best of 0.9R. The ceiling of two wide weeks is the maximum, not the grade: a cup with violent weeks inside it is a B- base.
failures.stopped: stopped 4 sessions after the buy, 2016-12-22, low 256.36

failures.why: a 30-week, 23%-deep cup with an 8-day handle sitting on the 50-day; the breakout day closed in the lower third of its range (270.71 against a 273.63 buy), then the stock fell straight through the stop the next day (best 0.0R) and later broke out again from a lower pivot. A cup over 6 months old with the handle resting on the 50-day is a late, tired base; the base-count rule is the filter the scan cannot apply.
failures.stopped: stopped the next session, 2021-09-23, low 264.55; the breakout day closed in the lower third

failures.why: gapped over the pivot at the open, filled at the open and never traded above that fill in the window (best 0.0R); KMI 2016-09-08 did the same. A gap through a cup pivot without follow-through is what the chase limit (C28) and the 30-minute gap rule (B20) are there for.

examples.limits: Daily bars, weeks counted as 5 sessions. Base count, the real RS rating and group, the market reading, the 2.5x-the-index ceiling and the bear-market 50% allowance are not in the scan. Stops are evaluated on daily lows. Best R is the high before the stop, not a realised trade. ARCB 2023-07-18 (best 78R) was left out of the ten because its stop was 0.29% under the buy. Nothing here is a published statistic.

near_misses.why: cup 6.6% deep; the rule needs 12% to 35%. A shallow shelf, closer to a flat base.
cup 20 sessions (4.0 weeks); the rule needs 35 sessions (7 weeks). A four-week dip, not a cup.
handle lows rise +0.53 a day (a wedge); the rule needs flat or down. A wedging handle with no shakeout.
12% of the cup's bars have lows in the bottom quarter; the rule needs 30%. A V, not a U.

conflicts: Depth, from the high or from the advance: IBD, Zanger and AAII 2001 measure the fall from the old high (12% to 35%); StockCharts and AAII 2015 measure a third of the prior advance. The card measures from the high (D-052).

Depth ceiling: IBD alone gives 33%, 35% and 30% or 35% in different columns, plus 50% in bear markets; Zanger 20% to 35%; the scanner 12% to 35%; Chart IQ 15% to 50%; the classical cup 12% to 50%. The card takes 12% to 33% with 33% to 35% graded down and 50% only in a bear market (D-052).

Cup length: IBD 7 to 65 weeks (one column says 6); Zanger 8 to 12 weeks; StockCharts 1 to 6 months; AAII 2001 one month in bull markets to 12 in bear markets; the scanner caps at 65 daily bars (13 weeks). The card takes 7 to 65 weeks (D-051).

Handle depth: IBD usually 8% to 12%; Zanger about 5% below the old high; AAII 2001 a third of the cup's depth, at most half; the scanner half the cup's depth (up to 17.5%). The card takes 12% with 8% and 5% as grades (D-053).

Handle position: IBD and Bulkowski upper half; AAII 2001 not into the lower half; AAII 2015 upper half or third; Minervini's one post describes a handle in the upper third of one chart. The card gates on IBD's midpoint test and grades the upper third.

Handle length: IBD at least 5 days and more than one or two weeks; Bulkowski at least 1 week, no maximum, under his 22-day median better; Zanger 4 days to 3 weeks; AAII and StockCharts 1 to 4 weeks; the scanner 5 to 15 bars and rejects a handle whose low is in its last 30%, which IBD praises as a shakeout. The card takes 5 sessions as the floor and 22 as the grade-down.

The trigger: IBD and Zanger buy as price trades through the handle high (IBD adds 10 cents); Bulkowski and AAII use a close above the rim; the scanner a close on 1.5x the 20-bar volume. The house buys at market as it trades through (E57); the cent, the dime or at market is D-003.

Breakout volume: IBD 40% to 50% above average (once calling 38% barely sufficient); AAII 50% over the 50-day; Zanger's ZVR; the scanner's 1.5x the 20-bar average. The card makes 1.4x the 50-day a warning and a grade, not a gate (D-006). The scan's light-volume winners (GWW, EFX) and heavy-volume loser (BX) say the same.

The stop: IBD 7% to 8% below cost (4% in a weak market); Bulkowski the handle low; the scanner the handle low times 0.985 (8.2% and 16.1% in the probe); Zanger, StockCharts and AAII give none. The house day's-low stop within about 3% wins, with the handle low as the outer limit (D-008).

Exits: IBD sells most at 20% to 25% and holds 8 weeks after a fast 20%; Bulkowski 61% of the cup height; StockCharts and AAII the full cup height; the scanner the full height. The house thirds win. Whether C33's 10-day time stop gives cups more time is D-019.

Prior-trend window: the dossier measures 30% over 120 sessions (6 months, the screener's window); the glossary's canonical base window is 65 sessions (dossier 01). The card keeps 120 and says so; the question bank treats the two windows as the same test.
Tightness: the glossary's default is a 0.85 range ratio; this card keeps the dossier's fixed 3% spread of the last 5 handle closes, listed as an override under tight.

Early entries: Minervini's 3-C and Bulkowski's handle trendline buy before the pivot; IBD's handle columns buy at the pivot; the owner's mid range cheat and in-handle shakeouts are his execution. The card teaches the pivot as the definition and the in-handle buy as execution, the cheat as a separate advanced lesson (D-027).

The scanner's stacked gate (close above the 10-day, 20-day, 50-day and 200-day) is stricter than any source and, with the 13-week cap, likely explains why it fires on 2 of 2,890 symbols; its narrative carries unsourced claims (Zanger's highest-edge setup, 18-28% deep cups, since the 1960s, 1.5x to 3x the projection) that D-010 removes.

The 100 draft bank cup items: 40 have handles under 5 sessions, 20 were under the 200-day, 9 are deeper than 33%, 5 are shorter than 35 sessions. They are rebuilt from this card before any go live (D-004, D-007).

The screener's IBD-style cup (bc:cup-with-handle) had its member drawing withdrawn on 2026-10-24 after a blind recertification; two of its code comments (no IBD minimum handle length) are contradicted by IBD's five-day floor.

Bulkowski's site carries a notice against use for AI training; his numbers are cited with links and short quotes only. He ranks the cup 3rd of 39 on his hindsight measure and 11th in his fixed-holding table.
